newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada 1996 job insurance payments falling - Martin.
newsitem.headline: Canada 1996 job insurance payments falling - Martin.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Wednesday changes his government had introduced to the employment insurance premium rate and maximum insurable earnings level since 1994 would reduce employee and employer contributions by C$1.8 billion in 1996.
"This is a significant reduction in payroll taxes that will lead to lower labor costs and increased employment," Martin said in his autumn budget, delivered in parliament.
He fell short of annnouncing any specific cuts in employment insurance premiums in the near future.

Martin has come under pressure from politicians and businesses to introduce some form of tax cut in his next budget. A cut in employment insurance premiums would effectively be a business tax cut and could help create more jobs.
Canada's economy, has been recovering steadily in the second half of 1996, but the unemployment rate has remained stubbornly high. The jobless rate stood at 9.4 percent in August.
